newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Swatch to use Card technology.
newsitem.headline: Swatch to use Card technology.

text.p: Card Technologies Australia Ltd said on Tuesday that its CiT smart card technology would be included in the Swatch Access watch, giving the watch payment access via a computer chip and antenna.
The company said it had entered into a marketing agreement following the completion of development of the new watch.
It said the product would be trialed in western Sydney in September and launched later this year.
"Swatch has incorporated a computer chip and a radio communications antenna into the Swatch Access watch," Card said.

"Using the CiT System multi-application software, the Swatch Access watch will be able to be used as a normal watch, as an electronic purse cash substitute payment system, as an access control device, as a ticket, will operate loyalty and incentive programs for merchants and may be used as a substitute for membership cards," it said.
"The watch will have all the functionality of the CiT Transcard product developed by Card Tech, in addition to being a watch."
Swatch is owned by Swiss watchmaker Ste Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie SA.
Share trading in Card Technologies was halted before the market opened on Tuesday, pending an announcement.
Its shares rose four cents after trading resumed to 83 cents, valuing the company at A$28.19 million based on 33.97 million shares outstanding.
Card Technologies listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in June following a share offer pitched at 30 cents each and underwritten by Prudential Bache Securities.
